correctness.rationale: Deleting closed endpoint neighborhoods gives Z=I_n+z, the two single-site numerators zI_(n−2), and joint z²I_(n−4). The recurrence roots a,b satisfy a+b=1 and ab=−z and yield I_(n−4)I_n−I_(n−2)^2=(−1)^(n−1)z^(n−2). Thus odd n is positive, and for even n the positive-coefficient ratio I_(n−4)/z^(n−3) strictly decreases from infinity to zero. At z=1 it equals one only for n=4; at z=2 it is below one. For z<2, I_(m+2)/I_m>a²>z² for even m, forcing strict ordering of successive roots, and a/z>1 gives convergence to 2. In the log root equation the left factor is log(a/z)=(2−z)/3+O((2−z)^2), and the right tends to log(3/2), with characteristic-ratio error O(2^(−n)). This verifies the stated first-order asymptotic and error. A separate conditional-deletion enumeration classified all 1,099 graphs and 10,650 marked pairs, giving exactly 60 mixed-sign numerators, all z³−z⁴ and all marked fans. There is also an analytic cross-check from Bencs: a reversal requires both parities of induced u–v paths. Through five vertices this requires an induced P4 and a common neighbor outside it (an induced length-four path on five vertices is the entire graph and cannot coexist with another path). If k of the two possible common-neighbor-to-internal-vertex edges are absent, the connected induced bipartite terms give z³+(k−1)z⁴, since each absent edge permits one positive four-vertex term and the P4 is the only negative term. The full five-vertex induced graph has an odd cycle. Only k=0 reverses, giving precisely K1∨P4 with the marked endpoints.
residual_risks: The large-fan result is for path endpoints and a common positive activity, not site-dependent fugacities or all vertex pairs. The minimum counts total graph vertices, while n indexes only the path.

evidence: Bencs expands the marked-pair difference over induced connected bipartite graphs, with a sign from marked distance and a squared partition polynomial for the complement of the closed neighborhood. Trinks proves a parity-graph sign property for the unweighted independent-set count.
broader_coverage.reasoning: On a fan, the hub-containing terms require an independent set of additional internal path vertices, so they sum to +z³I_(n−4) for covariance. The only hub-free term is the full path with sign (−1)^(n−1). Thus Bencs directly covers the displayed covariance identity and the special rational example. Fixed-parity signs also apply for odd path sizes, but not to the competition between the two parities on even fans.

Trinks also reports the marked F4's zero at unit activity as a minimal Merrifield–Simmons counterexample. Credit those facts explicitly. The distinct combined result is the all-activity minimum and uniqueness of strict sign reversal, together with the even-fan sequence of unique thresholds, its strict increase and its sharp approach to 2. The compared works do not resolve that positive-activity classification and threshold law.
residual_risks: Gutman's 1990 Graph propagators is known through Trinks and Bencs citations here; the 2001 Wang–Li–Gutman full text was not retrieved. Older chemical graph theory may contain further overlapping special cases. No historical priority is asserted.

value.rationale: A monotone fugacity can switch the sign of a two-site hard-core correlation even on a five-vertex graph; distinguishing this from a zero at one fugacity is substantive. The classification resolves the smallest possible competition of opposite-parity induced paths, and the fan sequence quantifies how that competition gives a strictly varying threshold converging to 2 with an explicit leading constant. This adds information beyond evaluating a classical identity or rechecking a known unit-weight counterexample.
residual_risks: The activity limit is a finite-graph crossover sequence, not an infinite-volume thermodynamic phase transition or a general classification of larger graphs.
